clips.send: Opium War and Treaty of Nanjing. 1840—1842. The beginning of China’s modern history. June 1839: the official Lin Zexu (林则徐 Lín Zéxú) destroyed confiscated opium on the beach at Humen (虎门 Hǔmén), near Guangzhou — a heavy blow to opium smuggling. June 1840: using the Humen opium destruction as an excuse, Britain launched the Opium War. August 1842: the Qing government was forced to sign the Treaty of Nanjing: cede Hong Kong Island to Britain; pay 21 million silver dollars; open Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai as treaty ports; tariffs on British goods had to be agreed with Britain. Impact: China began to sink into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society. The Opium War marks the start of China’s modern history.

clips.send: Eight-Nation Alliance and Boxer Protocol. 1900—1901. China became a fully semi-colonial, semi-feudal society. The Boxers (义和团 Yìhétuán) rose against foreign powers under the slogan “Support the Qing, wipe out the foreigners”. 1900: Britain, the USA, Russia, Japan, France, Germany, Italy and Austria formed an allied army, took Tianjin and Beijing. 1901 Boxer Protocol: pay 450 million taels of silver, guaranteed by customs and other taxes; the Legation Quarter at Dongjiaominxiang with foreign guards and no Chinese residents; destroy the Dagu forts and let foreign troops be stationed along the Beijing–Shanhaiguan railway; strictly forbid anti-imperialist activities. Impact: the Qing became a “court of the foreigners”; China completely sank into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society.

clips.send: New Culture Movement. From 1915. A movement that liberated people’s thinking. 1915: Chen Duxiu (陈独秀 Chén Dúxiù) founded Youth Magazine in Shanghai (renamed New Youth, 新青年 Xīn Qīngnián, from Vol. 2), launching the movement. Leaders: Chen Duxiu, Li Dazhao, Lu Xun, Hu Shi and others; Peking University became one of its centres. Content: promote democracy, oppose autocracy; promote science, oppose ignorance; promote new morality, oppose old morality; promote new literature, oppose old literature. Hu Shi wrote “Suggestions for the Reform of Literature”; Lu Xun published the first vernacular short story, “A Madman’s Diary”. Later, Li Dazhao and others spread Marxism; the movement freed people’s minds and prepared the ground for Marxism in China.

clips.send: 1911 Revolution. 1911—1912. Overthrew the autocratic monarchy. Sun Yat-sen (孙中山 Sūn Zhōngshān) founded the Revive China Society (1894) and the Tongmenghui (同盟会 Tóngménghuì, the “Revolutionary Alliance”) in Tokyo (1905), whose programme — expel the Manchu rulers, restore China, found a republic, equalise land rights — became the Three Principles of the People (nationalism, democracy, people’s livelihood). 10 October 1911: the Wuchang Uprising broke out and province after province responded. 1 January 1912: Sun Yat-sen took office in Nanjing as Provisional President — the Republic of China was founded. The Qing emperor abdicated in February. March 1912: the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China — the first law in Chinese history with the nature of a bourgeois-republican constitution. Significance: it ended more than 2,000 years of autocratic monarchy and spread the idea of a democratic republic — but Yuan Shikai seized the fruits of the revolution.

clips.send: Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. 1851—1864. The peak of China’s old-style peasant wars. 1851: Hong Xiuquan (洪秀全 Hóng Xiùquán) launched the Jintian Uprising in Guiping, Guangxi, and founded the “Taiping Heavenly Kingdom” (太平天国 Tàipíng Tiānguó, “Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace”). 1853: the Taiping army took Nanjing, renamed it Tianjing (天京, “Heavenly Capital”) and made it the capital; it issued the Heavenly Land System, a plan to share out farmland equally. 1859: Hong Rengan put forward A New Work for Aid in Administration, the first fairly systematic plan in modern China for developing capitalism. After the Tianjing Incident (1856) it declined; Tianjing fell in 1864 and the movement failed. Significance: it dealt heavy blows to Qing rule and to foreign aggressors.

clips.send: Second Opium War. 1856—1860. Anglo-French forces burned the Old Summer Palace. Supported by Russia and the USA, Britain and France launched the Second Opium War to open China’s market further. 1858 Treaty of Tianjin: foreign envoys to live in Beijing; ten more ports including Hankou and Nanjing; foreign merchant ships and warships free to sail the Yangtze ports. 1860: the Anglo-French army took Beijing, looted and burned the Old Summer Palace (圆明园 Yuánmíngyuán), the emperors’ garden palace. Convention of Peking: Tianjin opened as a port; the Kowloon area ceded to Britain. Taking advantage of the war, Tsarist Russia seized more than 1.5 million square kilometers of Chinese territory in the northeast and northwest. Impact: China’s semi-colonial status deepened further.

clips.send: Self-Strengthening Movement. 1860s—1890s. Learning Western technology: “self-strengthening” (自强 zìqiáng) and “seeking wealth” (求富 qiúfù). Leaders: Prince Gong (Yixin) at court; Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang and Zhang Zhidong in the provinces. Guiding idea: “Chinese learning as the foundation, Western learning for practical use.”. Early stage, slogan “self-strengthening”: military industries such as the Anqing Arsenal, the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Fuzhou Navy Yard. Later stage, slogan “seeking wealth”: civilian industries such as the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company and the Hanyang Iron Works; also new navies such as the Beiyang Fleet, new-style schools and students sent abroad. The Beiyang Fleet’s total defeat in the Sino-Japanese War marked its failure, but it brought in Western technology and China’s first modern enterprises — it is seen as the start of China’s modernisation.

clips.send: Hundred Days’ Reform. 1898. Reformists tried to build a constitutional monarchy. 1895: Kang Youwei and the provincial graduates in Beijing for the exam petitioned the emperor — the “Gongche Petition” (公车上书 gōngchē shàngshū). 11 June 1898: Emperor Guangxu issued the edict “Defining the State Policy” and launched the reform. Measures: reform government offices and appoint reformers; encourage private mines and factories; open new schools, drop the “eight-legged essay” (a rigid essay form used in the old exams), found the Imperial University of Peking; train a new army and navy. 21 September: Empress Dowager Cixi staged a coup and the reform failed; Tan Sitong and the other “Six Gentlemen” were killed. It lasted 103 days. Significance: a patriotic political movement and an ideological enlightenment.

clips.send: Sino-Japanese War and Treaty of Shimonoseki. 1894—1895. Greatly deepened China’s semi-colonial status. 1894: Japan provoked the war. In the Battle of the Yellow Sea, Deng Shichang (邓世昌 Dèng Shìchāng), captain of the warship Zhiyuan, died a hero. Early 1895: the Beiyang Fleet was completely destroyed at Weihaiwei. April 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki: cede the Liaodong Peninsula, Taiwan with all its affiliated islands, and the Penghu Islands to Japan; pay 200 million taels of silver; open Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou and Hangzhou; allow Japan to open factories in treaty ports. Under pressure from Russia, Germany and France, Japan returned the Liaodong Peninsula, but China paid 30 million taels to “redeem” it. After the war the powers began a scramble to carve up China.

clips.send: 太平天国运动。1851—1864。中国旧式农民战争的最高峰。1851年，洪秀全在广西桂平金田村发动起义，建号“太平天国”。1853年，太平军攻占南京，改名天京，定为都城；颁布《天朝田亩制度》。1859年，洪仁玕提出《资政新篇》，这是中国近代第一个比较系统的发展资本主义的方案。1856年天京变乱后由盛转衰；1864年天京陷落，太平天国运动失败。意义：沉重打击了清朝的统治和外国侵略势力。

clips.send: 戊戌变法。1898。资产阶级维新派的改良运动。1895年，康有为联合在北京参加会试的举人上书光绪帝，史称“公车上书”。1898年6月11日，光绪帝颁布“明定国是”诏书，宣布变法。内容：改革政府机构，任用维新人士；鼓励私人兴办工矿企业；开办新式学堂，废除八股文，开办京师大学堂；训练新式陆海军等。9月21日，慈禧太后发动政变，变法失败，谭嗣同等“戊戌六君子”遇害。变法历时103天，史称“百日维新”。意义：是一次爱国救亡的政治运动，也是一次思想启蒙运动。

clips.send: 甲午中日战争与《马关条约》。1894—1895。大大加深了中国半殖民地化程度。1894年日本挑起甲午战争；黄海海战中，致远舰管带邓世昌壮烈牺牲。1895年初，北洋舰队在威海卫战役中全军覆没。1895年4月《马关条约》：割辽东半岛、台湾全岛及所有附属各岛屿、澎湖列岛给日本；赔偿日本军费白银2亿两；开放沙市、重庆、苏州、杭州为商埠；允许日本在通商口岸开设工厂。在俄、德、法干涉下，日本归还辽东半岛，但清政府另付白银3000万两“赎辽费”。甲午战争后，列强掀起瓜分中国的狂潮。

clips.send: 第二次鸦片战争。1856—1860。英法联军火烧圆明园。英、法两国在俄、美的支持下发动第二次鸦片战争，目的是进一步打开中国市场。1858年《天津条约》：外国公使进驻北京；增开汉口、南京等10处为通商口岸；外国商船和军舰可以在长江各口岸自由航行。1860年，英法联军攻占北京，洗劫并火烧圆明园。《北京条约》：增开天津为商埠，割九龙司地方一区给英国。沙俄趁火打劫，先后侵占中国东北和西北150多万平方千米领土。影响：中国半殖民地化程度进一步加深。

clips.send: 鸦片战争与《南京条约》。1840—1842。中国近代史的开端。1839年6月，林则徐主持虎门销烟，沉重打击了鸦片走私。1840年6月，英国以虎门销烟为借口，发动鸦片战争。1842年8月，清政府被迫签订《南京条约》：割香港岛给英国；赔款2100万银元；开放广州、厦门、福州、宁波、上海五处为通商口岸；英商进出口货物缴纳的税款，中国须同英国商定。影响：中国开始沦为半殖民地半封建社会。鸦片战争是中国近代史的开端。

clips.send: 洋务运动。19世纪60—90年代。学习西方先进技术：“自强”“求富”。代表人物：中央有奕䜣，地方有曾国藩、李鸿章、左宗棠、张之洞等。指导思想：“中学为体，西学为用”。前期以“自强”为口号，创办军事工业，如安庆内军械所、江南制造总局、福州船政局。后期以“求富”为口号，创办民用工业，如轮船招商局、汉阳铁厂；还筹划海防，建立北洋水师等新式海军，创办新式学堂，派遣留学生。甲午战争中北洋舰队全军覆没，标志着洋务运动失败；但它引进了西方先进技术，使中国出现了第一批近代企业，被视为中国近代化的开端。

clips.send: 新文化运动。1915年起。一场思想解放运动。1915年，陈独秀在上海创办《青年杂志》（第二卷起改名《新青年》），新文化运动兴起。代表人物：陈独秀、李大钊、鲁迅、胡适等；北京大学成为运动的中心之一。主要内容：提倡民主，反对专制；提倡科学，反对愚昧；提倡新道德，反对旧道德；提倡新文学，反对旧文学。胡适发表《文学改良刍议》；鲁迅发表第一篇白话小说《狂人日记》。后期，李大钊等宣传马克思主义；运动促进了思想解放，为马克思主义在中国的传播创造了条件。
